glossary.definition: Measure of the tendency of an atom to attract a bonding pair of electrons.
Energy required to remove an electron from a gaseous atom or ion.
Distance from the center of the nucleus to the boundary of the electron cloud.
Time for half of a radioactive substance to decay.
Different structural forms of the same element in the same physical state.
Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons.
Distinct state of matter with uniform properties (solid, liquid, gas, plasma).
Distribution of electrons in atomic orbitals.
Hypothetical charge an atom would have if all bonds were 100% ionic.
Arrangement of atoms in a crystalline solid.
Regular repeating arrangement of points in space representing atomic positions.
Energy difference between the top of the valence band and the bottom of the conduction band.
Quantity that determines the magnetic force on a moving electric charge.
Amount of heat per unit mass required to raise the temperature by one degree.
Rate at which heat passes through a material.
Mass per unit volume of a substance.
Temperature at which a solid becomes a liquid.
Temperature at which a liquid becomes a gas.
Change in enthalpy when one mole of a compound is formed from its elements.
Energy change when an electron is added to a neutral atom.
